heroHeadline: Day 68: Trump Says Iran Deal 'Very Possible,' War 'Over Quickly' as Tehran Reviews US Proposal; Cuba Sanctions EO Signed
heroSubtitle: On May 7, 2026 (Day 68 of the US-Iran war), President Trump expressed strong optimism that a peace deal with Iran was imminent — stating 'it's very possible we'll make a deal' and that the war would be 'over quickly' — as Iran actively reviewed the latest US proposal via Pakistan's diplomatic back-channel. Iran submitted its own 14-point counter-proposal on May 2 demanding war termination within 30 days, security guarantees, an end to the naval blockade, release of $6B in frozen assets, war reparations, and lifting of sanctions. The Hormuz ceasefire held on Day 68 while the US naval blockade of Iranian ports remained active (41 tankers, ~69M barrels blocked). Brent crude continued easing to ~$97–101/bbl on diplomatic optimism. Trump also signed an Executive Order (Federal Register 2026-09173) on May 7 imposing a new sanctions framework against Cuban regime officials for political repression and threats to US national security — citing Cuba's alignment with Iran, harboring of foreign intelligence operations near US territory, and destabilizing migration. White House Border Czar Tom Homan pledged 'mass deportations are coming' at the Phoenix Border Security Expo, highlighting ICE's ~1,200 daily arrests ahead of the Senate's $72B ICE/CBP reconciliation vote the week of May 11. Kevin Warsh's full Senate floor confirmation vote as Fed Chairman remains set for that same week, before Jerome Powell exits May 15.
